title: Add calibration rationale for 3-second typing rate limit
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md
Line: 931

Current text:
  "Servers SHOULD rate-limit `Chat/typing` calls per account per chat. Servers SHOULD accept no more than one call per account per chat per 3 seconds; calls that exceed this rate MAY be silently discarded without error."

This is already SHOULD + specific number, which is the right shape. What's missing is the *rationale* — readers see "3 seconds" with no explanation of why that value rather than 1 or 10 or 30. Adding the rationale converts an arbitrary-looking number into a calibrated default and tells implementers what trade-offs they're making if they deviate.

Suggested addition (one sentence appended to the existing text, or a new sentence immediately after):

  "Servers SHOULD rate-limit `Chat/typing` calls per account per chat. Servers SHOULD accept no more than one call per account per chat per 3 seconds; calls that exceed this rate MAY be silently discarded without error.

  The recommended 3-second value pairs with the 10-second client-side decay timer described later in this section: with one accepted event per 3 seconds while a sender is actively typing, the receiver's decay timer sees at least three events before deciding the sender has stopped. Servers using a significantly lower rate impose unnecessary load on themselves and on federated peers; servers using a significantly higher rate risk receivers clearing the typing indicator while the sender is still active."

This bead is paired with T3-1 (jmap-chat-spec-ic5s.1). Recommend doing both in one commit so the cross-references resolve correctly and the calibration arguments stay consistent.
acceptance_criteria:
- The existing SHOULD + 3-second wording is retained unchanged
- A rationale paragraph follows, naming the 10s decay pairing
- The federation-load and receiver-misbehavior consequences of significant deviation are both named
- The text reads as guidance, not new normative requirement
